company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex to expand meaningfully into the fast-growing Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll reported solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have still beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS of 42 cents still cleared consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no immediate financial impact disclosed.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against the Street's 13.85% estimate, despite revenue coming in slightly above at $2.311 billion vs. the Street's $2.17 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a ~75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The results are a significant positive catalyst for the company as it competes in the high-growth GLP-1 obesity drug market. This positions VKTX as a meaningful contender in the space dominated by larger pharma players.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open — let's run through them.

Starting with AutoZone. They beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at fifty-six dollars and five cents against the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents. But here's the problem — the beat was low quality. It was driven by a one hundred forty-five basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a one hundred five basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out and the picture gets less impressive. Domestic comps missed badly — up one point six percent versus the Street at three point one percent — and the operating expense ratio worsened one hundred basis points year-over-year. Management did note that sales improved in the back eight weeks of the quarter versus the first eight weeks, and they expressed confidence heading into fiscal twenty-seven. Expect the stock to face pressure on the comp miss.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront plus another one hundred six and a half million. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a strategic move into Physical AI and robotics — a high-growth area — and should be read as bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid beat on fiscal first quarter earnings — fifty-three cents versus the Street's thirty-six cents — and the quality held up. Even excluding an eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind, they would have earned forty-two cents, still well above consensus. Sales did miss though, down three point three percent organically to nine hundred twenty-three million versus the Street's nine forty-three. Orders rose three point five percent year-over-year. Fiscal twenty-seven sales guidance was trimmed modestly, but the earnings per share range of one eighty-five to two fifteen was left unchanged. Call it mixed with a slight lean positive given the earnings quality.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November first. He brings prior chief financial officer experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. Routine leadership transition — not a major market mover.

THOR Industries missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — seventy-eight cents versus the Street's eighty-seven cents. Gross margins were the culprit, falling two hundred thirty basis points year-over-year to twelve point four percent against an estimate of thirteen point eight five. Management's tone was cautious — citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure weighing on consumer budgets. They expect a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal twenty-seven and won't provide formal guidance until later in the fall. There were some positives — dealer inventory is clean, structural cost actions are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly seventy-five percent year-over-year. But the headline miss and cautious tone will weigh on the stock.

Finally, the big mover this morning — Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing twenty-two percent weight loss. That is a significant result and puts Viking firmly on the map as a real competitor in the obesity drug space. This is the clearest bullish catalyst of the morning.

Bottom line: VKTX is the standout mover to the upside. THOR and AZO face selling pressure. Cognex's RealSense deal is strategically sound. Stay nimble.
